# Now 2.11.3
- Full-screen lyrics now size themselves to the screen so about eight lines are visible at once — matching Apple Music — instead of the line count and font drifting with display size. - Larger, more generously spaced lyric type and a slightly larger album art in the full-screen view for a closer match to Apple Music. - The native window buttons (close / minimize / zoom) now slide down from the top of the full-screen view when you move the pointer up, so you can close or minimize without pressing Escape. The red button still exits cleanly and leaves the desktop overlay running.

# Now 2.11.2
- Full-screen lyrics now use the whole screen like Apple Music: album art and controls sit centered in the left half (title, progress, and buttons aligned to the artwork), lyrics fill the right half, with a clear gutter between. With no lyrics, the art and controls simply center on screen. - Larger, uniform lyric type so a comfortable number of lines is visible at once, with the active line emphasized by brightness and weight and kept near the middle. - Tightened lyric timing in the full-screen view: the active line is now tracked at 30 Hz (previously ~5 Hz), so the highlight follows the vocal much more closely instead of lagging behind it.

# Now 2.11.1
- The full-screen view now opens as a true macOS full-screen Space with the standard zoom animation (growing out of the overlay), so a three-finger swipe moves between it and your previous window — with the desktop overlay still waiting on the original Space. - Lyrics now animate like Apple Music: the current line sits bright and bold about a third from the top, sung lines rise and fade away, and the next line springs into focus, with distant lines gently dimmed and blurred for depth. - Smoother, more alive motion throughout — spring-based lyric scrolling, an artwork crossfade on track changes, and an animated play/pause button.
